sections.html:
Burien is a King County suburb of 51,859 people (July 1, 2025), on Puget Sound just south of Seattle and west of Seattle-Tacoma International Airport. Owners live in 56.6 percent of homes here, and the middle owner-occupied home is worth $638,800. Roughly 34 percent of residents speak another language at home, so the city issues its renting handbook in both English and Spanish. Your choices are an agent, a sale by owner, or cash from a buyer who accepts the house as it stands.

sections.h2: Parts of Burien that shape appeal
sections.html:
Burien borders Seattle and the unincorporated communities of White Center and Boulevard Park on the north, Tukwila and SeaTac on the east, and Normandy Park on the south. Where your house sits within that frame changes how buyers describe it.

  • Olde Burien surrounds Southwest 152nd Street on the west side of Ambaum Boulevard, and Town Square holds shops, condominiums, apartments, a senior living center, a King County library branch and City Hall.
  • Ambaum Boulevard follows the old Lake Burien Railway route.
  • Lake Burien is a state-owned water body ringed by private property with no public access, so describe lakefront views and access carefully.
  • Three Tree Point lies just west of town.

The Highline School District serves Burien, with Highline High School, Big Picture, CHOICE Academy and the Puget Sound Skills Center. Confirm the assignment for your exact address before quoting a school.

Burien sits at the junction of State Routes 509 and 518, northwest of the airport, and Ambaum Boulevard and Des Moines Memorial Drive carry traffic north. King County Metro and Sound Transit buses leave the Burien Transit Center for Seattle, Bellevue, the airport, West Seattle, Kent, Auburn, Renton, Des Moines and Tukwila. Mean commute is 26.7 minutes. Buyers who work near the airport or downtown Seattle weigh that against price, so lead with the transit and freeway access when you describe the house.

sections.h2: Rental rules when a tenant lives there
sections.html:
Burien requires an annual rental housing business license, handled by the state Business Licensing Service, but single-family residences, condos, townhomes, manufactured homes and accessory dwelling units are exempt. For other rentals, the 2026 fee per complex is $323.80 for 1 to 10 units, $809.50 for 11 to 50 units and $971.41 for 51 or more.

  • Under the Rental Housing Policy in BMC 5.63, a landlord needs one of a list of just causes to evict, and wanting to sell the unit counts only after the tenant gets at least 90 days' written notice.
  • A landlord cannot evict from a unit that lacks a required license, or whose required inspection was not finished by the deadline.
  • The inspection program, in place since 2021, requires at least 20 percent of covered units to be inspected every three years.
  • Owners of buildings with five or more units that rent at affordable levels must give the city 60 calendar days' written notice before listing the building for sale.

State law also limits rent increases (RCW 59.18.700 and 59.18.720). The city's rental housing program answers questions at (206) 241-4647.

sections.h2: Excise tax and disclosure at closing
sections.html:
The seller pays the real estate excise tax. RCW 82.45.060 scales the state share with price, and the county treasurer tacks on the local portion when the affidavit comes in. Starting January 1, 2027 the break points move up to $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000. Burien's median value sits above the first band, so a typical sale pays two rates.

A finished disclosure statement is the other deliverable. RCW 64.06.020 gives you five business days from mutual acceptance of the contract, and it excuses the form when the buyer waives it or the transfer is exempt. After delivery, the buyer may rescind within three business days. The form covers title, water, structural items, systems and fixtures and environmental questions, so gather permits and repair records before you start.

Under RCW 84.56.020 the halves fall due April 30 and October 31. A home with four or fewer units that falls behind accrues nine percent interest a year, with no penalty. King County Treasury Operations can quote today's balance before you list. Every tax statement also describes the senior and disabled exemption (RCW 84.36.379 through 84.36.389) and the deferral program in chapter 84.38 RCW.

sections.h2: Your options for a quick sale
sections.html:
A seller with a tight timeline, a tenant in place or a house that needs work usually compares three routes.

  • List with an agent, which suits a vacant house in good condition.
  • Handle the sale yourself, including the disclosure form and the excise tax affidavit.
  • Request a cash offer, useful when repairs, an inheritance or a tenant's notice period are slowing things down.

Whatever you pick, read the notice rules in BMC 5.63 before you ask a tenant to leave, and build the 90 day notice period into your schedule.

sections.h2: What to gather before you list
sections.html: Pull together the permits and repair records that the disclosure form asks about, since it covers title, water, structural items, systems and fixtures. If a tenant lives in the house, add the lease and a copy of the written notice you plan to give. The notice rules in BMC 5.63 and the 90 day minimum come first, because a sale date set before the notice runs out can fall apart. For a rental building with five or more units at affordable rents, remember the 60 calendar day notice to the city before listing. The rental housing program at (206) 241-4647 can confirm which rules cover your property.

Start with the paperwork: permits, repair records, the tenant's lease and notice, and your tax statement. Next comes the disclosure form, then the offer. Escrow runs title work and prorates taxes, and you sign the affidavit and deed. With cash there is no loan approval to wait for, so title work and any tenant notice period set your date. Keep your tax statement, permit records and tenant paperwork in one folder so escrow can move the day title is ordered, and ask the treasurer about any balance well before closing.

faqs.q: Does a Burien single-family rental need the city rental housing license?
faqs.a: No. Burien exempts single-family residences, condominiums, townhomes, manufactured homes and accessory dwelling units from the annual rental housing business license. The eviction and notice rules in BMC 5.63 can still apply.

faqs.q: Can I end a tenancy in Burien because I am selling the house?
faqs.a: Yes, but only with at least 90 days' written notice, because selling the unit is one of the just causes in BMC 5.63.070. Without a valid cause, the city rules do not allow the eviction.

faqs.q: How is state excise tax figured on a Burien sale?
faqs.a: The state rate is graduated, and the median-priced home spans the first two bands. The county treasurer adds the local portion, and escrow gives you the exact total.

faqs.q: What must a Burien seller give the buyer?
faqs.a: A completed disclosure statement. Deliver it within five business days of mutual acceptance, though a buyer can waive it and some transfers are exempt. Rescission is open to the buyer for three business days afterward.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Burien?
faqs.a: April 30 and October 31. Overdue tax on a home of four or fewer units earns nine percent interest a year.
